To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the majority vote with independent classifiers is not necessarily better than the individual classifier; 2) negative pairwise dependence is not necessarily detrimental for the accuracy; 3) the highest improvement over the individual classifier can be achieved when all pairs of classifiers are dependent in the same direction (either positive or negative); and 4) the improvement can be dramatic, up to 100% for the majority vote with two dependent classifiers, compared to the individual classifier with accuracy 1/2.
the majority vote can be much better than the best individual classifier and the improvement depends on the pairwise dependence between individual classifiers.
